claims.exact_statement: There exist two controlled three-daughter branching models with exactly identical CLE drift b(x,a) and covariance A(x,a) at every full observable state and for every action, yet opposite action rankings for safe founder reach. The laws nu1=(1,3,3,1)/8, nu2=(1,9,3,3)/16, and nu2rev=(3,3,9,1)/16 all have E[K]=3/2 and E[K^2]=3, so with a common division rate lambda the actionwise fields are b=lambda*r*(1/2,3/2) and A=lambda*r*diag(1,3). Swapping nu2 and nu2rev across the B action changes P(K=3) from 3/16 to 1/16 while preserving all fields.
assumptions: The full observable state is the R and U cell-count vector (and may include clone-labelled counts); only R cells divide.
At each action a, each R parent is replaced at the same unknown common rate lambda in both worlds by three exchangeable daughters with offspring count K from the action-specific law.
Offspring draws are independent across parent events; the three laws have the same first and second raw jump moments.
Safe reach for one generation is K=3 and unsafe-any is K<3.
claims.status: internally derived exact controlled CLE-equivalence counterexample; verified with exact rational arithmetic; no biological validation or novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Uses the existing Cycle 2 b=3 pairwise-independent offspring laws and standard CLE jump-moment formulas; Cycle 3 is a controlled coefficient-equality application, not a new branching theorem.
claims.costs: No data needed for the construction. Biological application requires randomized founder clones, full sister outcome histograms, division-time/rate tracking, and semantically valid endpoint assays.
claims.falsifier: An algebraic contradiction under the listed offspring laws would falsify the construction; biological relevance is falsified if no feasible intervention pair matches division rate and first two offspring moments while separating the higher-order family law.
claims.next_gate: Demonstrate two feasible schedules with matched division rate, E[K], and E[K^2] but separated higher-order K law; then validate on held-out randomized lineages.

claims.exact_statement: For the strict CLE-equivalent models in CLG3-1, if W-plus uses reporter sensitivity/false-positive rates 0.9/0.1 and W-minus uses 0.1/0.9, and the B offspring law in W-minus is the coordinatewise complement of W-plus, then every observed daughter-label vector has exactly the same law in both worlds. The common division rate is the same under both actions and in both worlds, so event times match and all finite/multigeneration lineage transcripts remain identical under any adaptive policy although the safe-reach action ranking reverses; worst-case ranking error is at least 1/2.
assumptions: W-minus uses the mirrored offspring law for each action relative to W-plus.
W-plus reporter sensitivity/false-positive rates are 0.9/0.1 and W-minus rates are 0.1/0.9.
Reporter emissions are not externally calibrated or semantically anchored.
All observed event times and censoring are retained; the common division rate lambda is identical between worlds and actions.
claims.status: internally derived exact observational-equivalence proof; not biological validation
claims.novelty_boundary: A model-specific construction using standard hidden-state label symmetry; no new general HMM identifiability theorem is claimed.
claims.costs: No finite sample count resolves an exact alias. A gold-standard endpoint/emission calibration or an orthogonal functional endpoint is required.
claims.falsifier: A calibrated semantic anchor or an observed variable with different conditional laws in the two models invalidates the stated observation interface and can distinguish the worlds.
claims.next_gate: Use action- and context-matched gold-standard R/U references to bound the emission matrix orientation and error.

claims.exact_statement: For two randomized independent-founder arms with directly observed binary safe-reach endpoint and true mean gap Delta, Hoeffding gives ranking error at most exp(-n Delta^2); for the strict witness gap Delta=1/16 and alpha=0.05, n=767 founders per action suffices. With known independent per-daughter sensitivity 0.9/false-positive rate 0.1, the product deconvolution score has range width 405/256 and n=1920 founders per action suffices for the same true endpoint ranking.
assumptions: Founder clones are the independent sampling units.
Assignment is randomized, endpoints are bounded and correctly classified, and the action-specific population/context is fixed.
The ranking gap is positive and known for the bound; there is no unmodeled interference.
For the noisy-label bound, reporter errors are independent across daughters conditional on their true fates and the calibrated per-daughter channel has sensitivity 0.9 and false-positive rate 0.1.
claims.status: internally derived concentration bound and arithmetic check; not a biological power calculation
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Hoeffding bounds; no statistical-method novelty is claimed.
claims.costs: Counts independent founder clones; donor/organoid blocks, lineage imaging, reporter calibration, exposure measurement, and censoring follow-up are additional costs.
claims.falsifier: Dependence between purported independent founders, action-specific reporter drift, or misclassified endpoints invalidates the nominal bound.
claims.next_gate: Pilot donor-level dependence, endpoint noise, and event rates before assigning an organoid-scale sample budget.

claims.exact_statement: Known or calibrated binary endpoint emissions with positive contrast permit inversion p=(q-f)/(s-f); if s-f is bounded below by kappa0 and treatment/calibration proportions each have error at most gamma<=kappa0/4, plug-in probability error is at most 4 gamma/kappa0.
assumptions: A gold-standard semantic R/U reference is available for calibration.
The same calibration channel applies to treated observations, or calibration is stratified by every action/type/context affecting emissions.
claims.status: internally derived deterministic inversion/error bound from Hoeffding-calibrated proportions
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary confusion-matrix inversion and concentration; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: Requires n_cal >= ceil(log(4/alpha_cal)/(2 gamma^2)) gold-standard examples for each of R and U, plus the treated founder sample and any needed action/type/context strata.
claims.falsifier: Unknown semantic orientation, contrast near zero, or emission drift outside calibrated strata prevents the bound from applying.
claims.next_gate: Measure action- and phenotype-stratified confusion rates with orthogonal truth labels.

claims.exact_statement: For an exchangeable three-daughter law K in {0,1,2,3}, once normalization and E[K], E[K^2] are fixed, one scalar such as P(K=3) or E[K(K-1)(K-2)] determines the remaining one-dimensional offspring-count family. In the witness, this statistic separates nu1, nu2, and nu2rev despite identical first and second moments.
assumptions: The daughter outcomes are exchangeable, so their joint law is determined by the count law of K.
The support is exactly contained in {0,1,2,3}.
The first two count moments are known or tested equivalent.
claims.status: internally derived finite-dimensional linear-algebra fact; standard and no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Specific finite-support moment identification; no new moment-problem theorem is claimed.
claims.costs: Requires paired/triple daughter fate classification per founder division; aggregate single-cell marginals or pair covariance are insufficient.
claims.falsifier: An exchangeable four-point distribution family with the stated fixed moments and two distinct laws sharing P(K=3) would falsify the uniqueness statement.
claims.next_gate: Estimate the full daughter-count histogram in matched-moment, held-out action arms.
